newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares edge up, flotations sideline traders.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares edge up, flotations sideline traders.

text.p: Egyptian share prices inched upwards in sluggish Tuesday trading as state privatisation announcements kept investors shy of the market.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 0.17 points higher at 234.29 after shares worth an average 19.89 pounds ($5.85 million) were traded.
"It was another slow day and the millers were again the highlight but the privatisation offers are slowing trading," said broker Youssef Khalil of Delta Stockbrokers.
Earlier, the state said it was offering private investors a majority 51 percent stake in subsidiary Development and Popular Housing Company.

It had also promised to float another stake in partly private Cairo Housing and Development in addition to offering investors up to 30 percent of Central and West Delta Flour Mills which brokers forecast would sell well.

Milling shares continued to dominate the bourse activity with Central Egypt Flour Mills, the day's most active share, rallying up to 29 pounds in midsession on rumours it had increased net profits for 1995/96 by 30 percent.
North Cairo Flour Mills was also heavily traded but closed 0.76 pounds down at 94.24 pounds.
Recently privatised Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals fell 2.15 pounds in heavy turnover, mainly on slow transactions by the bourse's computer system.
"It's unbearably slow, out of every 10 buy or sell orders you put in, it only accepts one. Buyers and sellers met through the system by chance," Khalil added.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 337.53 from a 17-month high of 338.57 points on Monday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 160.69 points from 160.00.
Gaining stocks outnumbered losers 18 to 14 while another 18 firms were traded but ended unchanged.
